narrative.overview:
An Israeli voter drops a printed slip in an envelope; the count turns slips into 120 seats; 61 is a government. The system makes that arithmetic the identity: a grid of 120 squares with one heavy rule meaning 61, and party cards drawn as ballot slips with real Hebrew letters. Everything else is paper and two inks (black for display, numbers, rules and selected states; dark grey for prose), set ragged right on one left edge.

Colour is never decoration. The four bloc colours mark bloc context; each list's editorial colour (lib/party-colors.ts) owns that list's surfaces and figures; a shared ordinal ramp shows where a stance sits on an issue. A page with no data on it is black and white.

Density is a reference work's: figures sit beside the sentences they illustrate, every number dated and sourced, sources folded one tap away at the foot.
keyCharacteristics: 120-seat grid, 12 across, heavy rule under row five so the next cell is the 61st.
Party cards are ballot slips: square sheet, hairline edge, colour bar on top, Hebrew letters in Frank Ruhl 900.
Frank Ruhl Libre carries display, numbers and reading prose; Public Sans carries labels, controls, tables and captions.
Square, flat paper; 4px only on controls; one drawer shadow in the whole system.
Colour appears only where it encodes data.

rules.name: The Colour Is Data Rule
rules.body: A colour appears only where it encodes a bloc, a list or a stance position. Chrome, headings, links and buttons are ink.

rules.name: The Fixed Endpoints Rule
rules.body: Ramps and tints use fixed endpoints (stance-ramp-start/end, tint-base), not theme variables, so a shade means one thing in light, dark and print. The Compare matrix draws the same ramp with the same endpoints, so one answer has one shade wherever it appears; the shade is the answer's place in its issue's order from one end of the debate to the other.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: No all-caps labels and no tracking-out. Labels are Public Sans 600 13px, sentence case.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Every number that can be compared (tables, meters, seat counts, glance figures, source list markers) uses tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Plain Headline Rule
rules.body: Headlines carry no eyebrow above them and no single accented word.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: Sheets, slips, tiles, panels and grid cells take no shadow. Lift is a hairline (line-2) on sheet white; hover is the hairline turning ink.

rules.name: The 61 Rule
rules.body: The only heavy rule in the system is the majority line: 2.4 units in the seat grid, a 2px ink tick at 61/120 in the majority bar and the polls bloc bar, and the 2px tick at 61 on each bloc strip axis. A heavy rule anywhere else is wrong.

rules.name: The Pull Quote Rule
rules.body: The only left-edge colour rule is the 3px party-colour rule on a pull quote (ink when no party colour applies). Slips and party letter boxes carry their colour as a top bar instead (5px slip, 4px compare chip and drawer letters).

rules.name: The Mark Tells The Series Rule
rules.body: In article charts a series is told apart by its mark (solid, ring, grey diamond, grey ring) and position, in ink and greys, never by colour or dashes; dashed means absent. Heat shades use the fixed endpoints #2a2925 over #f6f5f1 up to 62%, with text black or white by luminance (threshold 0.179).

dos: Do draw any count of the Knesset as the 120-seat grid or a 120-seat bar, with the heavy ink rule at 61.
Do keep colour to data: bloc colours for blocs, the list's own colour for that list, the stance ramp for stance positions.
Do pick text on a party or bloc fill by luminance (partyInk or the `-ink` tokens).
Do set every page head as title, then standfirst, inside the 1200px wrapper on the shared left edge.
Do put a figure beside the sentences it illustrates, with a label on an ink rule and a dated source line.
Do use 0 radius on paper and 4px on controls.
Do fold sources into the end-of-page disclosure, open by default on single-subject pages.
Do use dashed strokes to mean absent, out or reference.
Do shade a stance by its place in the issue's order, with the same ramp everywhere an answer appears.
donts: Don't set labels in all caps or tracked-out caps.
Don't put an eyebrow or kicker above a headline.
Don't build meta lines as middle-dot strings.
Don't number items (01/02/03) unless the content is a sequence; list slot numbers and source citations are data, not markers.
Don't draw a heavy rule that does not mean 61.
Don't use a coloured left rule anywhere but the 3px party-colour rule on a pull quote.
Don't add shadows to paper; the drawer is the only shadow.
Don't draw the Knesset as a hemicycle.
Don't colour chrome, headings or buttons.
